The build is complete and verified. Here's the acceptance report.

**The application is ready for you to use at → http://maker:4000**

It's the real, working software (not a prototype): genuine page-reading for auto-fill, a real database that remembers everything across visits, real single-file page/PDF preservation, and the actual public Internet-Archive submission. Your collection starts empty — add a link, or use **Settings → Import** to bring in a browser bookmarks file.

**What I verified.** I checked the software against every behaviour we agreed on, at two levels — automated checks of the underlying logic and automated checks that drive the real screen the way you would. **All of them pass.** In plain terms, confirmed working:

- **Saving** — paste a link, details are read from the page automatically, adjust title/description, add tags (with suggestions), a formatted note, and "read later"; saving a link you already have opens the existing one instead of duplicating; a page that can't be read still saves manually; non-links are refused.
- **Finding** — search across everything with the full language (`#tag`, `"phrases"`, `AND/OR/NOT`, parentheses, clear error on a bad query); browse by tag from the bar or a card, combined with search; sort with a remembered default.
- **Read later** — a separate view; "mark as read" removes it there but keeps it in the collection.
- **Managing** — edit any field, permanent delete with confirmation, click a card to open it; archive vs delete with its own restorable view; select many (or all matching) and tag/read/archive/delete together.
- **Preserving** — a private preserved copy (self-contained page, or the PDF itself), and a separate public Internet-Archive submission behind a confirmation.
- **Filters & data** — save named search+include/exclude-tag filters; import/export the standard bookmarks file (archived kept in an "Archived" folder, imports never overwrite your details).
- **Display** — default sort, items-per-page, and text size in Settings, all remembered.

Recorded for a **later cycle** (not in this build): a native mobile experience, and automatic preservation.

Please try it at **http://maker:4000**. **Do you accept this software and agree to complete this cycle?** If anything doesn't behave as we agreed, tell me and I'll treat it as a correction within this cycle; a request for *new* behaviour I'll record for the next cycle.
